Convert thresholds to the scale of the plot axis

Source: R/scale-conversion.R
to_plot_scale.Rd

Thresholds are defined on the scale of an effect-size metric; estimates are often plotted on another scale (raw mean differences, odds ratios). to_plot_scale() converts thresholds to the axis on which the estimates are drawn. geom_es_zones() and geom_mcid_zones() call it for you; use it directly to inspect the boundaries that will be drawn.

Usage

to_plot_scale(thresholds, sd = NULL, scale = c("identity", "log"))

Arguments

thresholds

An es_thresholds() or mcid_thresholds() object.

sd

Standard deviation used for conversion between standardised and raw units, or NULL.

scale

"identity" (additive zones, null +/- cut) or "log" (multiplicative zones, null * cut and null / cut).

Value

An object of the same class with converted thresholds. The scale element records whether zones are additive or multiplicative and note describes the conversion.

Effect-size thresholds

  • d with sd: cuts are multiplied by sd to give raw differences. Which SD to use is a substantive choice; for contrasts from a linear model the residual SD (pooled_sd()) is the usual one, but a baseline or reference-population SD may be more appropriate.

  • d with scale = "log": cuts are converted to odds ratios with log(OR) = d * pi / sqrt(3) (Chinn 2000). This is an approximation that assumes an underlying logistic distribution; it is not the same mapping as es_benchmarks("chen_or").

  • or/rr with scale = "log": zones are symmetric on the log scale around the null: a cut c gives boundaries null / c and null * c. Use with null = 1 and a log axis (e.g. ggplot2::scale_x_log10()).

  • or/rr with scale = "identity": for an axis showing log ratios on a linear scale; cuts become -log(c) and log(c) around null = 0.

  • r, eta2, f: drawn on their own scale only. There is no conversion to raw differences.

MCID thresholds

MCIDs are already on the raw scale. If sd is given they are divided by it, for an axis showing standardised differences.

References

Chinn S (2000). A simple method for converting an odds ratio to effect size for use in meta-analysis. Statistics in Medicine 19(22):3127-3131.

Examples

to_plot_scale(es_benchmarks("cohen_d"), sd = 2)
#> <es_thresholds> on the "raw" scale
#> negligible: |effect| in [0, 0.4)
#> small: |effect| in [0.4, 1)
#> medium: |effect| in [1, 1.6)
#> large: |effect| in [1.6, Inf)
#> Source: Cohen J (1988). Statistical Power Analysis for the Behavioral Sciences,
#> 2nd ed. Hillsdale, NJ: Lawrence Erlbaum. Cohen offered these values as
#> conventions for use only when no better basis for judging magnitude is
#> available.
#> Note: d cut-points multiplied by SD = 2.
to_plot_scale(es_benchmarks("cohen_d"), scale = "log")
#> <es_thresholds> on the "or" scale
#> negligible: |effect| in [1, 1.44)
#> small: |effect| in [1.44, 2.48)
#> medium: |effect| in [2.48, 4.27)
#> large: |effect| in [4.27, Inf)
#> Source: Cohen J (1988). Statistical Power Analysis for the Behavioral Sciences,
#> 2nd ed. Hillsdale, NJ: Lawrence Erlbaum. Cohen offered these values as
#> conventions for use only when no better basis for judging magnitude is
#> available.
#> Note: Approximation: log(OR) = d * pi / sqrt(3) (Chinn 2000), which assumes a
#> logistic latent variable.
to_plot_scale(es_benchmarks("chen_or"), scale = "log")
#> <es_thresholds> on the "or" scale
#> negligible: |effect| in [1, 1.68)
#> small: |effect| in [1.68, 3.47)
#> medium: |effect| in [3.47, 6.71)
#> large: |effect| in [6.71, Inf)
#> Source: Chen H, Cohen P, Chen S (2010). How big is a big odds ratio?
#> Interpreting the magnitudes of odds ratios in epidemiological studies.
#> Communications in Statistics - Simulation and Computation 39(4):860-864. These
#> odds ratios correspond to d = 0.2, 0.5 and 0.8 only when the event rate in the
#> reference group is 1%; the equivalent odds ratios are smaller at higher
#> baseline risks.
#> Note: Zones symmetric on the log scale: boundaries at null / c and null * c.
